description:
## Outcome

One reusable harness unpacks a target archive in an isolated test root and verifies the packaged product without Erlang or Elixir on `PATH`.

## Work

1. Accept an archive, expected target, and expected version as explicit inputs.
2. unpack under a path with spaces and under a non-ASCII profile path.
3. Build a minimal `PATH` with no system `erl`, `elixir`, or `mix` and prove the launcher still runs.
4. Check version and help commands, a provider-free local scenario, exit statuses `0`, `1`, and `64`, daemon lifecycle, restart persistence, and no-daemon behavior.
5. Validate layout, metadata, notices, file permissions or access controls, and private runtime selection.
6. Capture diagnostics separately and reject unexpected secret or host-path data.
7. Emit machine-readable test evidence for CI.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The same harness runs on macOS, Linux, and Windows.
- [ ] It fails if the launcher finds a system OTP or misses packaged runtime data.
- [ ] It fails on a partial JSONL line or an ambiguous local run artifact state.
- [ ] It never calls a live model provider.
- [ ] It distinguishes automated checks from the manual TUI checklist.
- [ ] Failures identify the target and exact acceptance check.

## Tests

Test the harness with known-good synthetic packages and packages with removed runtime, bad metadata, bad permissions, corrupt JSONL, and wrong exits.

## Non-goals

Do not duplicate the local output-directory lifecycle owned by `jido_cli-tqg.6.4`. Do not claim a pseudo-terminal is full TUI acceptance.
title: Build a hermetic packaged-artifact acceptance harness
